decisions.reason: Changing the Title style font size does not alter the PBU naming prefix, language, applicability, or covered style categories.
The Title font-size parameter changes within the typography requirement, while the obligation to apply the style system consistently across all templates remains unchanged.
The source changes the Title style to 28 pt and does not change bullet dimensions, scaling, alignment, or approved appearance.
The Title font-size decision does not change the required stability or predictability of content copied from legacy templates.
The source does not alter Tab-key level transitions, list applicability, hierarchy structure, or nested-list alignment.
Changing the Title font size does not alter the requirement that pasted content remain within column and page boundaries.
The source concerns the Title style only and does not change numbered-list or multi-digit alignment behavior.
The Title font-size change does not affect the required ability to insert manual line breaks after pasted content.
The source does not change table paste stability, right-column boundaries, or the existing unresolved table-adjustment conflict.
The typography adjustment does not change the supported Word for Windows environment or the operational-reliability requirement.
The Title font-size change does not alter document language, default language, or style-name language configuration.
